chunks.title: Production VPC Layout — Multi-AZ Public/Private Subnets with Per-AZ NAT
chunks.content:
Production VPC Layout — Multi-AZ Public/Private Subnets with Per-AZ NAT

Provisions a production VPC with DNS support and hostnames enabled, an Internet Gateway, and one public and one private subnet per availability zone (CIDRs derived deterministically via cidrsubnet). Public subnets set map_public_ip_on_launch=true and route 0.0.0.0/0 to the Internet Gateway; private subnets have no public IPs and route 0.0.0.0/0 to a per-AZ NAT Gateway (each with its own Elastic IP). The AZ list, VPC CIDR (default 10.0.0.0/16), region, and environment are variables.

When to use:
- Use as the network foundation for multi-AZ production workloads that need public ingress/egress (load balancers, NAT) and private application/data tiers
- Use the availability_zones list variable to control how many AZs (and therefore subnets and NAT gateways) are created

Best practices:
- Derive subnet CIDRs with cidrsubnet(var.vpc_cidr, 8, index) so subnets are non-overlapping and deterministic across AZs
- Deploy one NAT Gateway (and one Elastic IP) per AZ so a single AZ failure does not cut outbound access for the other AZs; associate each private subnet with its own per-AZ private route table
- Enable enable_dns_support and enable_dns_hostnames on the VPC, and tag every resource with Environment, Tier (public/private), and ManagedBy=terraform

Security considerations:
- Keep map_public_ip_on_launch=false on private subnets so application and data tiers never receive public IPs
- Place only internet-facing resources in public subnets; private subnets reach the internet only outbound through NAT, with no inbound path from the IGW

Terraform resources: aws_vpc (DNS on) + aws_internet_gateway + aws_subnet.public/private (count over AZs, cidrsubnet) + aws_eip.nat + aws_nat_gateway (per AZ, depends_on IGW) + aws_route_table public(IGW)/private(NAT) + associations.

chunks.title: VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch
chunks.content:
VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch

Enables VPC Flow Logs capturing ALL traffic for the VPC and delivering them to a dedicated CloudWatch Log Group (retention 30 days). A dedicated IAM role assumable by vpc-flow-logs.amazonaws.com grants the logs:CreateLogGroup/CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents/DescribeLogGroups/DescribeLogStreams actions needed to write the logs.

When to use:
- Use as a security and network-observability baseline so VPC traffic (accepted and rejected) is recorded for audit, troubleshooting, and threat detection

Best practices:
- Capture traffic_type ALL (not just ACCEPT or REJECT) for complete visibility
- Set an explicit CloudWatch log retention (30 days here) so logs are kept long enough to investigate without growing unbounded
- Use a dedicated flow-log IAM role rather than reusing an unrelated role

Security considerations:
- Flow logs provide the network-visibility signal needed to detect and scope intrusions and misconfigurations
- The flow-log role's logs policy uses Resource "*"; tightening it to the specific log group ARN would further enforce least privilege

Terraform resources: aws_flow_log (traffic_type ALL → CloudWatch) + aws_cloudwatch_log_group (/aws/vpc-flow-log/${env}, retention 30) + aws_iam_role flow_log (assume by vpc-flow-logs.amazonaws.com) + aws_iam_role_policy (logs:* actions, Resource "*").
